think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 58-year-old HIV-infected male who discontinued antiretroviral therapy presented with acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nocturnal fevers, recent urethral discharge, and an anterior perihepatic fluid collection on ultrasound, mimicking isolated Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome, but accompanied by diffuse splenic microabscesses and intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy diagnostic of concomitant splenic tuberculosis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Stops after presentation, history of ART discontinuation, vital signs, physical exam showing RUQ tenderness, baseline labs (WBC 18,000, microcytic anemia, elevated CRP/ESR, CD4 250, viral load 16,000, normal chest radiograph), and abdominal ultrasound demonstrating perihepatic pseudoseptated fluid, intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly with diffuse parenchymal microabscesses, before anti-tubercular therapy initiation.
3. Differential Distinctions: Isolated Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (chlamydial or gonococcal perihepatitis) explains right hypochondrial pain and perihepatic pseudoseptated effusions following urethritis, but cannot account for parenchymal splenic microabscesses or prominent abdominal lymphadenopathy. Disseminated candidiasis, bartonellosis, or lymphoma can produce splenic microlesions in advanced HIV, but subacute nocturnal fevers, high local prevalence, and response to four-drug therapy establish splenic tuberculosis co-occurring with sexually acquired perihepatitis.
case_prompt: A 58-year-old male, married with three children, diagnosed with HIV infection 12 years earlier, presented complaining of right upper quadrant abdominal pain of 5 days' duration associated with vespero-nocturnal fevers, chills, and diaphoresis. He reported no cough, nausea, vomiting, or other gastrointestinal symptoms. He had received triple antiretroviral therapy since his HIV diagnosis but had voluntarily discontinued all medications 7 months prior without a specific reason; he had no prior history of opportunistic infections. Three days prior to presentation, he noted two episodes of purulent urethral discharge accompanied by dysuria; he was sexually active exclusively with his wife and denied high-risk sexual contacts. His CD4 count 8 months earlier had been 800/mm^3 with an undetectable viral load. On admission, he was in poor general condition, pale, and febrile with a body temperature of 37.7 C. Abdominal examination revealed tenderness in the right hypochondrium without a palpable mass or peritoneal signs; urethral discharge was no longer present, and the remainder of the physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory testing revealed a white blood cell count of 18,000 elements/mm^3 with 45% lymphocytes, microcytic anemia with hemoglobin 9 g/dL and MCV 72 fL, C-reactive protein of 25 mg/dL, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 70 mm/hr. His CD4 count was 250/mm^3 with a viral load of 16,000 copies/mL. Liver and renal function tests were normal, and plain chest radiography showed clear lung fields. Abdominal ultrasonography demonstrated an anterior perihepatic fluid collection between the hepatic capsule and the diaphragm containing fine pseudo-septa visualized with a high-frequency probe, enlarged intra-abdominal lymph nodes, and mild splenomegaly with multiple millimeter-sized hypoechoic microabscesses diffused throughout the splenic parenchyma.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Isolated Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome (FHCS) from sexually acquired perihepatitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Accounted for the right upper quadrant pain, recent purulent urethritis, and ultrasound findings of an anterior perihepatic fluid collection with pseudosepta. Ruled out as an isolated entity because it does not cause splenomegaly with diffuse parenchymal microabscesses or intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Cytobacteriological examination of urine was positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. Liver and kidney function tests were normal. The chest x-ray was also normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Disseminated opportunistic fungal microabscesses (Histoplasmosis / Candidiasis) or Lymphoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in an HIV-infected patient with treatment interruption and falling CD4 count presenting with multiple splenic lesions and lymphadenopathy. Ruled out in favor of splenic tuberculosis based on typical imaging and nocturnal constitutional symptoms.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The spleen was slightly increased in size with the presence of multiple microabscesses in the form of hypoechoic nodular lesions of millimeter-sizes diffused throughout the parenchyma and visualized with the high-frequency probe (Fig. 3 A-B).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Ultrasonic demonstration of diffuse millimeter-sized splenic parenchymal microabscesses and intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy in an immunocompromised patient with falling CD4 count alongside perihepatic pseudoseptated effusion, establishing the dual diagnosis of splenic tuberculosis associated with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Considering previous episodes of purulent urethral discharge, perihepatic effusion on ultrasound, diffuse splenic micro-abscesses and abdominal lymphadenopathy in the context of HIV-positive, the diagnosis of FHCS associated with splenic tuberculosis was retained.
